model_annotation: The image displays Figure 4, which consists of two stacked bar charts, (a) and (b), comparing the distribution of first-level semantic domains for two types of verbs—mainly auxiliary verbs and passive verbs—across four different text genres: news, traditional literature, online novels, and microblogs. The horizontal axis in both charts lists the four genres in a fixed order. The vertical axis represents frequency, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 2000, marked at intervals of 1000. In chart (a), "各语体中支配动词的一级语义域分布" (Distribution of first-level semantic domains of auxiliary verbs in various genres), the bars are segmented into multiple colored layers, each representing a specific semantic domain, with the total height of each bar indicating the total frequency of auxiliary verbs in that genre. The total frequencies are 562 for news, 478 for traditional literature, 1031 for online novels, and 1282 for microblogs. In chart (b), "各语体中承受动词的一级语义域分布" (Distribution of first-level semantic domains of passive verbs in various genres), the bars are similarly stacked by semantic domain, with total frequencies of 97 for news, 730 for traditional literature, 466 for online novels, and 545 for microblogs. The color of each segment corresponds to a specific semantic domain, as indicated by the legend in chart (b), which is not fully visible but is referenced in the text. The charts are arranged side-by-side, with (a) on the left and (b) on the right, allowing for a direct visual comparison of the semantic domain distributions for the two verb types across the same genres.
